newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu foes briefly occupy Zaire embassy in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu foes briefly occupy Zaire embassy in Paris.

text.p: Opponents of ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko briefly occupied Zaire's Paris embassy on Saturday and burnt a Zairean flag in support for rebels sweeping across the country, police said.

A group of about 50 protesters, who got in by simply ringing the doorbell of the building near the river Seine, left after about three hours. "The occupants left of their own accord," a police spokesman said.
Police said there were no arrests over the protest against Mobutu, who flew home on Friday from the French Riviera where he had been convalescing after prostate cancer surgery.
About 30 people kept up a demonstration in front of the building.
Embassy officials put up a new Zairean flag outside the building to replace one taken down and burnt. Protesters also took off a plaque on the wall of the embassy.

The protesters earlier said they were starting an indefinite occupation, declaring it the embassy of Congo-Kinshasa, in a show of support for rebel leader Laurent Kabila whose forces have captured a swathe of eastern Zaire.
France has been the strongest foreign supporter of Mobutu, 66, during his almost 32 years in power.
One embassy official, contacted by telephone, said that the protesters "rang the bell and we let them in. They took us by surprise...But they are not inside the embassy offices."
